react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct activity, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this metabolomics dataset. The five driver metabolites — testosterone (KEGG:C00535), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917), dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), and estrone (KEGG:C00468) — appear as metabolites_hit in run_ramp_enrichment's rank-0 pathway WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis, FDR 1.01×10⁻¹⁵, fold-enrichment 2,502×), in Mummichog's rank-0 pathway (C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism, p=3.36×10⁻⁴, overlap=13/13), and in MetaboAnalystR's sole KEGG hit hsa00140 (C21-Steroid Hormone Metabolism). These five compounds also annotate to WP:WP2263 (Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer), WP:WP5320 (Male steroid hormones in cardiomyocyte energy metabolism), and KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism), all sharing the same five-hit steroid cluster. RaMP also reports Reactome R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones, FDR 1.84×10⁻¹³) and R-HSA-193048 (Androgen biosynthesis, FDR 5.03×10⁻¹²). Coumarin (KEGG:C05851) independently hits Mummichog's Xenobiotics metabolism (p=0.038) but does not co-enrich with the steroid cluster. The remaining four compounds (spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) show no significant pathway membership across any paradigm. The cross-paradigm winner is C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism, a pathway that spans adrenal androgen synthesis through to androgen and estrogen interconversion, consistent with a treatment perturbation affecting steroidogenic flux.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis paradigms converge on steroid hormone pathway disruption in this metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis) as rank-0 with FDR 1.01e-15, hitting five steroid metabolites: 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone, KEGG:C03917), androst-4-ene-3,17-dione (androstenedione, KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), and dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227). The same five compounds co-annotate to WP:WP2263 (Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer, FDR 1.01e-15), WP:WP5320 (Male steroid hormones in cardiomyocyte energy metabolism, FDR 7.3e-15), KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism, FDR 2.95e-14), and REACT:R-HSA-193048 (Androgen biosynthesis, FDR 5.03e-12). Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently recovers the same cluster via MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p=3.36e-4, overlap 13/13) and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p=4.2e-4, overlap 12/12). Coumarin (KEGG:C05851) independently maps to Mummichog's MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism (p=0.043, overlap 2/2). Coumarin does not co-enrich with the steroid cluster, indicating a distinct xenobiotic signature. Spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, and doxycycline show no pathway membership across any paradigm, suggesting they are treatment-specific compounds or pharmacologic agents whose metabolic context is not captured by the current pathway libraries. The dominant biological signal is disruption of C21-steroid biosynthesis and interconversion, spanning adrenal androgen synthesis (DHEA) through androgen-to-estrogen aromatisation (estrone) and 5α-reduction (dihydrotestosterone).

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct activity, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in this metabolomics dataset. The five driver metabolites — testosterone (KEGG:C00535), androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917), dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), and estrone (KEGG:C00468) — appear as metabolites_hit in run_ramp_enrichment's rank-0 pathway WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis, FDR 1.01×10⁻¹⁵, fold-enrichment 2,502×), in Mummichog's rank-0 pathway (C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism, p=3.36×10⁻⁴, overlap=13/13), and in MetaboAnalystR's sole KEGG hit hsa00140 (C21-Steroid Hormone Metabolism). These five compounds also annotate to WP:WP2263 (Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer), WP:WP5320 (Male steroid hormones in cardiomyocyte energy metabolism), and KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism), all sharing the same five-hit steroid cluster. RaMP also reports Reactome R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones, FDR 1.84×10⁻¹³) and R-HSA-193048 (Androgen biosynthesis, FDR 5.03×10⁻¹²). Coumarin (KEGG:C05851) independently hits Mummichog's Xenobiotics metabolism (p=0.038) but does not co-enrich with the steroid cluster. The remaining four compounds (spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) show no significant pathway membership across any paradigm. The cross-paradigm winner is C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism, a pathway that spans adrenal androgen synthesis through to androgen and estrogen interconversion, consistent with a treatment perturbation affecting steroidogenic flux.
